events.title: John Calvin dies in Geneva
events.description: The French reformer died aged 54 in the city he had shaped into a Protestant model. His Institutes of the Christian Religion influenced Reformed churches from Scotland to the Netherlands.
events.html: The French reformer died aged 54 in the city he had shaped into a Protestant model. His Institutes of the Christian Religion influenced Reformed churches from Scotland to the Netherlands.

events.title: Peter the Great founds St Petersburg
events.description: Construction began on the Peter and Paul Fortress on an island in the Neva, on land newly taken from Sweden. Peter made the city his capital, Russia's 'window on Europe'.
events.html: Construction began on the Peter and Paul Fortress on an island in the Neva, on land newly taken from Sweden. Peter made the city his capital, Russia's 'window on Europe'.

events.title: Golden Gate Bridge opens to pedestrians
events.description: Some 200,000 people walked across the new bridge on its opening day before cars were allowed the next. Its main span was then the longest of any suspension bridge.
events.html: Some 200,000 people walked across the new bridge on its opening day before cars were allowed the next. Its main span was then the longest of any suspension bridge.

events.title: Royal Navy sinks the battleship Bismarck
events.description: Crippled by a torpedo hit to her rudder, Bismarck was pounded by British battleships and sank in the Atlantic. Only about 114 of her crew of over 2,000 survived.
events.html: Crippled by a torpedo hit to her rudder, Bismarck was pounded by British battleships and sank in the Atlantic. Only about 114 of her crew of over 2,000 survived.

events.title: Australians vote to include Aboriginal people in the census
events.description: Over 90 per cent voted to count Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in the population and to let the Commonwealth make laws for them. It remains Australia's most successful referendum.
